findings: Sequential two-stage patch chain verified: core2-report-contract-proposal/core2-report.patch applies cleanly as a purely additive patch to baseline/docs/CORE-STAGED-TESTS.md (at line 161) and baseline/openspec/changes/consolidated-language-kernel/specs/consolidated-language-kernel/spec.md (under UNI-018, UNI-020, and UNI-021), and core2-arena-contract-proposal/core2-arena.patch applies cleanly as a purely additive supplement against the exact virtual after-state of core2-report.patch (at line 235 of virtual CORE-STAGED-TESTS.md and line 212 of virtual spec.md under UNI-018) while preserving every baseline and first-stage line unchanged.

ADOPT M01 (core2-arena.patch decisions 1-5): (1) Whole Program for admitted language 'moriarty/2' retains exact seven fields (language:'moriarty/2', semantics:'moriarty-core/2', name, states, assets, expressions, actions) with category-filtered lexical declaration order and all actions (including unused actions) preserved, matching ir.rs and parser.rs::parse_profile(source, true). (2) StateDecl initializers, AssetDecl scale/identity, agreement/profile/action identifiers, Action.inputs (signature inputs in order followed by leading body input declarations), Await.binders, and statement metadata allocate zero arena nodes and introduce no synthetic statements. (3) Program.expressions is one global fresh-occurrence arena across all actions and statements in lexical order without resetting or rebasing at action/statement/await/segment boundaries, allocating children in left-to-right postorder (ExprId = current array length as u16) with no interning, constant folding, CSE, or grouping nodes for parentheses, and encoding LiabilityPresent/LiabilityAmount duty names as decoded string metadata rather than Literal child nodes. (4) Each statement allocates its single expression root (value, predicate, amount, or guard) at its lexical source position before pushing the Statement, with Await.guard allocated statically at parse time independent of runtime resume or event values. (5) The finite documented expression grammar and precedence (prefix not > * > +,- > ==,<,<=,>,>= > and > or, left-associative binary operators) match parser.rs::expr; PR203's two Core/1 fixtures are properly scoped as finite precedent without claiming general Core/1 grammar adoption or Core/1-Core/2 equivalence, and the undocumented parser token pair ('not','=') for BinaryOp::Ne is explicitly not canonized (nor is '!=' invented), leaving source inequality spelling/admission open for a separate grammar/source-repair decision.

ADOPT M02 (core2-report.patch decision 1): Site and capture layout contract matches stage/plan.rs, stage/mod.rs, stage/admit.rs, and runtime.rs. AwaitSite.site is the 1-based await occurrence per action (with site 0 and captures:[] representing idle entry/completion in PendingFrame), while AwaitSite.ordinal is the 0-based statement index in action.statements. StagePlan.actions preserves program declaration order and statement_count counts all source statements. CaptureSlot layout eagerly orders all action inputs (Origin::Input, 0-based input declaration ordinal) followed by preceding Let bindings (Origin::Let, 0-based statement ordinal) and earlier accepted Event binders (Origin::Event, 0-based originating Await statement ordinal, preserving binder declaration order) without liveness pruning, excluding state fields and the pending await's own binders. Runtime captures in PendingFrame and Continuation are ordered NamedValue {name, value} entries retaining binding-time values while state is read from the boundary.

ADOPT M04 (core2-report.patch decision 2): Per-statement Step attachment, typed values, complete snapshots, and effect deltas match runtime.rs::run_segment, execute_statement, and ir.rs. Every Step retains 0-based original action ordinal index, exact admitted IR statement with ExprId references, present typed outer Step.value, complete post-statement Snapshot (state BTreeMap, balances sorted by (asset, account), liabilities sorted by name including present-zero rows), and per-statement delta effects. Reaching an Await at start or after an accepted guard ends the segment before guard evaluation and emits no entry Step. A normal true resume begins its segment with one Await Step at the original statement ordinal carrying outer value {type:'Bool', value:true}, snapshot equal to execution.pre, and effects:[]. A normal false resume returns SegmentRun::NotAdvanced and projects segment:null with no public guard Step, value, effects, or synthetic snapshot. All other completed statements carry their exact typed evaluation result (Let RHS, Bool true for Requires/Ensures, Next RHS, Emit value, Transfer/Fee amount, Liability added amount, Discharge discharged amount) and single-statement effect delta (with Discharge using Effect::Liability {before, after} and retaining closing-zero liability rows in the snapshot), and Execution.effects is the ordered concatenation of Step deltas within that segment.

ADOPT M05 (core2-report.patch decision 3): Status envelope and DTO projection contract matches stage/report.rs::outcome_report, stage/mod.rs, and stage/admit.rs. Every root object is distinct from derived StageOutcome enum serialization and carries qualification:'local-reference-stage', authentication:'none', and consumption:'untracked'. Waiting roots project status:'waiting', advanced:true|false, segment (full StageSegment when advanced:true, explicit null when advanced:false), continuation (new Continuation when advanced:true, unchanged input Continuation when advanced:false), attempted, committed (projected from continuation.logical.committed), and residual (positive-amount liabilities from the boundary in name order). Complete roots project status:'complete', segment, attempted, committed, and residual, with advanced and continuation absent (not null) and frame_post idle (site 0, captures:[]). Rejected roots project status:'rejected', error, attempted, and committed, with advanced, segment, continuation, and residual absent, without selecting stage-specific error codes or admission precedence. StageLogical retains profile:'moriarty-reference-logical-cost/2', mandatory cap (UInt string or null, preserving input continuation.logical.cap on advancing waiting resume), and committed.

ADOPT M06 (core2-report.patch decision 4): Public CLI printing contract for ordinary waiting/complete simulate invocations matches simulate.rs::print_stage_result, core_io.rs::print, and json.rs::export. Output is one complete ASCII pretty JSON document on stdout followed by exactly one terminal LF, empty stderr, and exit 0: lexicographically sorted object keys (via serde_json::Value Map/BTreeMap), prescribed array order, 2-space indentation, compact {} and [] when empty, bare unsigned JSON integers for u16 and u8 scale, canonical decimal strings for UInt, standard short escapes plus lowercase \u0000-\u001f, \u007f, and UTF-16 \uXXXX escapes (including surrogate pairs) for non-ASCII scalars, within the 1 MiB bounded exporter limit. This public stdout contract is properly kept distinct from the stage_reports library pretty-byte check and the mori test multi-case aggregate report.

ADOPT M07 (core2-report.patch decision 5): Local logical cost schedule and committed-prefix reporting match stage/cost.rs, runtime.rs, and admit.rs. Profile moriarty-reference-logical-cost/2 charges 1 unit per statement dispatch plus 1 per distinct visited expression node with a fresh cache per statement and eager And/Or evaluation, 1 entry unit upon reaching the next await without evaluating its guard, and 1 dispatch unit plus distinct guard nodes upon resume. For n awaits, ActionPlan.segment_cost[0..=n], committed_before[j] = sum_{k<j} segment_cost[k] (with committed_before[0]=0), and plan_total = sum_{k=0..=n} segment_cost[k] match cost::fill. False guard resumes report attempted = dispatch_cost while keeping continuation.logical.committed unchanged; advancing segments report attempted = segment_cost[j] and committed = committed_before[j] + segment_cost[j]. The partial escrow freeze's 5/2/6 attempted and 5/5/11 committed numbers remain explicitly conditional pending recorded adoption and a separate new independent freeze.

Owner M03 boundary compatibility verified: The two proposals' treatment of program_hash and plan_hash as opaque String fields whose preimages/security properties were historical owner-UNASSESSED in the ordinary authoring lane is fully compatible with, and does not modify, the separate designated-owner adoption in identity-adoption/DESIGN-ADOPTION.json (which fixed local observational SHA-256 over recursively key-sorted compact UTF-8 JSON of the full 7-field Program and cost-filled StagePlan rendered as 64 lowercase hex characters). Adopting ordinary M01, M02, and M04-M07 supplies the remaining ordinary representation, layout, trace, envelope, rendering, and static-cost premises noted as pending in DESIGN-ADOPTION.json limits without encroaching on any designated-owner security, authentication, conservation, soundness, commitment, authorization, or ledger boundary.
limitations: All 14 original staged draft gaps (GAP-01 through GAP-14) remain individually OPEN; design adoption of M01, M02, and M04-M07 does not close any gap by inference or substitute for independent expectation freezes and actual runtime/consumer observations.
No parser, evaluator, CLI, Cargo, toolchain, SDK, or test command was executed; all Program, StagePlan, library, and CLI checks remain UNRUN.

No complete Program, StagePlan, Continuation, report envelope, or stdout byte goldens are invented or frozen by this review; a distinct independent custodian must derive and freeze unconditional expectations after recorded design adoption and status promotion.

The partial independent escrow oracle freeze (partial-independent-oracle/MISSING-PREMISES.json, DERIVATION.md, FREEZE.sha256) remains unchanged and read-only, and its 5/2/6 attempted and 5/5/11 committed work arithmetic remains conditional until recorded adoption and a separate subsequent freeze.

M01 is scoped strictly to the finite documented positive Core/2 grammar; it does not generalize PR203's two Core/1 fixtures into general Core/1 grammar authority or Core/1-Core/2 equivalence, and it does not canonize the undocumented 'not =' token sequence for BinaryOp::Ne or invent '!=' support.

This ordinary consumer review votes only on M01, M02, and M04-M07 and makes no authentication, conservation, soundness, commitment, authorization, cap/refusal-precedence, admission, security, or ledger decision; designated-owner M03 identity/security boundaries in identity-adoption/DESIGN-ADOPTION.json remain unmodified.
All Core/1 NR-01-06 and adopted financial-report obligations, as well as all U0-U7, M1-M17, MC/SP/G, mint/burn/accrual, ACTUS/DeFi, and composition roadmap obligations, remain open and unchanged.
